Social Studies.fw: Vermont College, Career, and Civic Life C3 Framework for Social Studies State Standards

std.D2.Civ.7.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Apply civic virtues when participating in school settings.
std.D2.His.9.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Identify different kinds of historical sources.
std.D2.His.10.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Explain how historical sources can be used to study the past.
std.D2.Civ.6.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Describe how communities work to accomplish common tasks, establish responsibilities, and fulfill roles of authority.
std.D2.Civ.2.K-2: Individually and with others, students… = Explain how all people, not just official leaders, play important roles in a community.
std.D2.Geo.8.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Compare how people in different types of communities use local and distant environments to meet their daily needs.
std.D2.His.3.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Generate questions about individuals and groups who have shaped a significant historical change.
std.D2.Geo.6.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Identify some cultural and environmental characteristics of specific places.
std.D2.Eco.3.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Describe the skills and knowledge required to produce certain goods and services.
std.D2.Eco.4.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Describe the goods and services that people in the local community produce and those that are produced in other communities.
std.D2.Geo.2.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Use maps, graphs, photographs, and other representations to describe places and the relationships and interactions that shape them.
std.D2.Geo.1.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Construct maps, graphs, and other representations of familiar places.
std.D2.Civ.5.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Explain what governments are and some of their functions.
std.D2.Geo.3.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Use maps, globes, and other simple geographic models to identify cultural and environmental characteristics of places.
std.D2.Eco.6.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Explain how people earn income.
std.D2.His.2.K-2: Individually and with others, students… Compare life in the past to life today.
std.D2.Civ.8.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Identify core civic virtues and democratic principles that guide government, society, and communities.
std.D2.Geo.5.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Explain how the cultural and environmental characteristics of places change over time.
std.D2.Civ.5.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Explain the origins, functions, and structure of different systems of government, including those created by the U.S. and state constitutions.
std.D2.Civ.1.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Distinguish the responsibilities and powers of government officials at various levels and branches of government and in different times and places.
std.D2.Geo.2.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Use maps, satellite images, photographs, and other representations to explain relationships between the locations of places and regions and their environmental characteristics.
std.D2.Civ.3.3-5: Individually and with others, students… Examine the origins and purposes of rules, laws, and key U.S. constitutional provisions.
